findings.summary: The refusal message leaves out the one remedy the reader can actually use, so a re-read of a records-measure reading cannot pass.
findings.evidence: The plan says the check's error message is the guidance (Decision 4); the reader re-reads once with it (reading.rs:732-740). The planned error offers two remedies: 'depend on job 20261030-070002-d103' or 'run the command on a fixture or a temp directory'. The reader cannot edit the request, so it cannot add the Depends line. For a code reading that changes a records measure, switching to a fixture makes check_records_measure, which runs earlier (checks.rs:541), refuse it, because that check requires a behavior criterion naming `real records` (surveys.rs:565-601). check_records_measure does not require `--snapshot`, so a criterion such as 'Run `athena status` on the real records ... expected range from history.json' passes that check and is then refused by the new one. The form that passes both checks, and that records_criteria.rs runs (records_criteria.rs:221-232), is `status --snapshot <evidence directory>`. The plan exempts it but never tells the reader. That is the job class (`status` on the real records) this request comes from. Fix: Make the error name three remedies: (a) for the request author, a 'Depends on 20261030-070002-d103' line; (b) for the reader, the command `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <evidence directory>`, which reads the evidence copy and not records/; (c) a fixture or temp directory. Assert `status --snapshot` in the error-text unit test (criterion 2 demonstration). Add a unit test of a code reading with a measure trigger: its plain `athena status ... real records ... expected range from history.json` criterion is refused by check_real_records_command, and the same reading rewritten as the error suggests (the `--snapshot` form) is accepted by refusing_check.
findings.location: Plan step 2 (the bail! text) and Decision 1; crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs:538-601

findings.summary: Three planned deliverables are left unchanged, and no step tells the producer to give a reason for each in its report.
findings.evidence: The accepted reading lists crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs as deliverables to modify. unchanged_planned_files sends the candidate back when a planned path is unchanged and the report's `unchanged_planned_files` gives no reason for it. Fix: Add to step 7 that the producer reports each of the three paths in `unchanged_planned_files`, with the reason from Decision 4 (reader budget 1998 of 2000, rule count pins, unchanged rule name).
findings.location: Plan step 7 ('leave briefs.rs, reader.rs and run_pin_tests.rs unchanged'); crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:1712-1729

findings.summary: The new changelog item could be mistaken for the scope-limit item by an existing test.
findings.evidence: scope_limit_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause takes the first Unreleased item containing `reading::check_scope_limit` and asserts scope-limit-specific needles in it. The plan's item describes the step's place 'after the scope-limit' check. If its text contains `reading::check_scope_limit` and it sits above the existing item, that test fails. Fix: State in step 7 that the new item does not contain the strings `reading::check_scope_limit` or `reading::check_records_measure`; refer to neighbours without the `reading::` path.

findings.summary: The lexical match has foreseeable false positives and false negatives that are neither tested nor named in the doc comment.
findings.evidence: False positive: the `-- <sub>` form only needs 'athena' somewhere in the criterion, so `cargo test -p athena-core -- plan` (a test-name filter; `-p athena-core` supplies 'athena') matches whenever the criterion also says 'real records'. False negatives: any one exemption word anywhere in the criterion clears it, so 'Run `athena status` on the real records, not a fixture' or '... and sample three jobs' passes. A bare 'Run `status` on the real records' (the shape at reading.rs:8452) is never matched because it names no athena. Fix: Require the `-- <sub>` form to follow an `athena-cli` package or binary (for example `-p athena-cli --` or `athena --`), not just any mention of athena. Treat an exemption word as one only when it names where the command runs (for example 'on a fixture', 'in a temp dir'), or drop 'sample'. Add unit cases for the cargo test filter and the 'not a fixture' negation, and list the remaining limits in the doc comment.

findings.summary: The sz3z shape is invented, but its corpus source says it was rebuilt from the job brief.
findings.evidence: A grep of the snapshot finds e5sg nowhere, and sz3z only in a job-id list (docs/design/agent-and-build-slots.md:300). The brief gives only the e5sg phrase. The plan admits the sz3z wording is a guess but labels the case 'rebuilt from the job brief'. Fix: Label the sz3z case source 'wording guessed; the request text is not in the snapshot', and give the gap as a limit in the doc comment and CHANGELOG, so a later job can replace the case with the recorded text.

findings.summary: `git status` shows nothing once the candidate is committed, so it does not show which files changed.
findings.evidence: The verifier's snapshot is a two-commit repository, base then candidate (run/mod.rs:2069). With the candidate committed, `git status` is clean whatever changed. Fix: Use `git diff --stat HEAD~1 HEAD` (or the snapshot's change list), and check that no path under records/, athena.toml, defaults.toml or .github/workflows/ appears.

summary: The plan adds `check_real_records_command` in surveys.rs as one step! line between check_scope_limit and check_boundary_and_repo_files. It exempts requests with a 'Depends on 20261030-070002-d103' line, read through dependency_ids_in, the same parser admission uses (topics.rs:376). Under unmet_dependency (plan.rs:404-436), that line counts as met once a retry of d103 lands. It adds unit tests and corpus cases. I checked the code it cites and it holds: the files, functions, helpers and line numbers exist. The `--snapshot` exclusion keeps every existing real-records criterion accepted (reading.rs:8350-8573, corpus 354/441, run/tests.rs:5617). No existing test criterion pairs an athena command with a real-records phrase; I grepped every crate. The chosen slot has no pinned neighbour (only reading.rs:8986 counts lines). The briefs.rs pins that read checks.rs look only at DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES, and nothing outside athena-core calls the gate. One design gap needs a revision. The plan makes the check's error message the guidance, and the reader gets one re-read, during which it cannot add a 'Depends on' line to the request. So the only remedy left in the planned error is 'use a fixture', and for a measure reading that makes check_records_measure (which runs earlier and requires `real records`) refuse the re-read. The form that works, `status --snapshot <evidence directory>`, which the plan itself exempts, is never named in the error. The other findings are minor: the untouched planned files need reasons in the producer report, changelog item placement, false positives and negatives of the lexical match, an invented sz3z shape, and a weak `git status` check for criterion 6. The plan makes no external service calls.
